note: Fictional story. Every character, company and broadcast in it is invented. The city issues it plays with are real.

chapters.title: OVERDUE
chapters.intro: They cut the library hours again, and somehow found millions for a ballpark. Take these petitions to City Hall before the clerk locks up.
chapters.outro: Four thousand signatures. Let them count those.
chapters.news: Port Gardner Radio news. Library hours are cut again as the city faces a budget gap. Officials say the downtown ballpark is still on schedule.

steps.text: Get the petitions to City Hall before the clerk leaves

chapters.title: DEMOLITION BY NEGLECT
chapters.intro: Lyle Pruitt buys old buildings and waits for the roof to fall in. Then he calls it progress. Post a preservation notice on three of his before he gets his permits.
chapters.outro: Now it is on the record. He can't say nobody told him.
chapters.news: Preservation notices appeared overnight on three downtown buildings owned by developer Lyle Pruitt. Pruitt called it vandalism with paperwork.

steps.text: Post a notice on the Culmback Building (1/3)
Post a notice on the Commerce Building (2/3)
Post a notice on the McCabe Building (3/3)

chapters.title: BALLPARK FIGURE
chapters.intro: Sam Reyes, Everett Ledger. The ballpark estimate went up again and nobody will show me the math. The numbers are in a contractor's truck by the station. Borrow it.
chapters.outro: Tens of millions over. That is some ballpark figure.
chapters.news: The Everett Ledger reports the ballpark estimate has grown by tens of millions. Mayor Dale Hargrove calls the number, quote, a rough ballpark figure.

steps.text: Take the contractor's box truck near Everett Station
Bring the truck to the Ledger office at the Evergreen Building

chapters.title: RIBBON CUTTING
chapters.intro: Congressman Whit Brannigan. I have three ribbon cuttings and one pair of scissors. The station, the port, then the arena. Drive. And smile, there are cameras.
chapters.outro: Democracy in action. Do not tell anyone how fast we went.
chapters.news: Congressman Whit Brannigan cut three ribbons in under six minutes today. His office is calling it a district record.

steps.text: Drive the congressman to Everett Station (1/3)
Last ribbon: Angel of the Winds Arena (3/3)

chapters.title: EYES ON BROADWAY
chapters.intro: The city put plate readers on every road into town. Fine. But who reads the logs? A friend at the service center has the audit. Get it, and lose whoever follows you.
chapters.outro: Every plate, every day, kept for a month. Front page.
chapters.news: Questions tonight about who can see the city's license plate camera logs. The police chief says the system is working as intended.

steps.text: Pick up the audit at the City Service Center
The cameras saw you. Lose the police
Bring the audit back to Sam at the courthouse

chapters.title: STRUCTURAL DEFICIT
chapters.intro: Pruitt is moving his cash out through the old mill site tonight. Gold coupe. Be a real shame if it ended up at the library instead.
chapters.outro: Well. That would keep the branches open on Sundays.
chapters.news: Developer Lyle Pruitt reports a gold coupe stolen from the old mill site. He declined to say what was in the trunk.

steps.text: Take Pruitt's gold coupe at the old mill site
Get the coupe to Marge at the library in one piece

chapters.title: PUBLIC COMMENT
chapters.intro: The council votes tonight. Mayor Hargrove wants it over before anyone reads the binder. Get to City Hall and sign up for public comment. Three minutes is all you get.
chapters.outro: Everett isn't broke. It was spending on the wrong things.
chapters.news: A surprise at City Hall tonight. The council tabled the ballpark vote after public comment ran four hours. Mayor Hargrove says he looks forward to further study.

steps.text: Get to City Hall before the vote. Every cop in town is looking for you
